rationale.conceptual: The method is an established but non-trivial MD approach (NPxxT ensemble with TIP4P and 9-3 LJ walls) requiring careful implementation of pressure control, wall potential, and thermodynamics analysis. It is not a routine 'compute a metric' task, but neither a novel custom algorithm. Understanding phase transition detection and Clapeyron equations is necessary.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has ~4-6 stages: setup, batch simulation loop (70 runs), equilibration/production, data aggregation, transition detection, and slope computation. Orchestrating many MD jobs is the main engineering burden, but the tooling (LAMMPS) is standard and I/O is straightforward.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running a series of NPxxT MD simulations of TIP4P water confined between hydrophobic walls, detecting phase transitions from pressure and energy profiles, and computing Clapeyron slopes. The conceptual difficulty is moderate: the method uses a well-known water model and standard MD ensemble, but implementing the lateral-pressure control, identifying transitions, and applying the confined-phase thermodynamics equations demands careful understanding. The execution involves orchestrating ~70 simulation runs (each 5+ ns) and a post-processing pipeline, but no exotic tooling or data handling. Resource needs are trivial: a 240-molecule system fits on a CPU with negligible memory.
